By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Will one of South Africa's best known stockbrokers is be remembered as South Africa's worst paedophile?

Summary:
Rich and powerful, stockbroker Sidney Frankel is being sued by 7 complainants who accuse him of having sexually abused them when they were children. Since the case became public, more victims have come forward, swelling the total to 24.

Further information:
Criminal charges of rape will be laid against Sidney Frankel. Because the offence is alleged to have happened over 20 years ago the complainant expects the prosecutor to decline to prosecute. When that happens the Sexual Offences Act of 2007 will be challenged in the Constitutional Court.

Extra Budget Items:
Travel to Cape Town to interview victims and to film the huts at Muizenberg beach, the site of many of the assaults
Travel to Hoedspruit to find Sidney Frankel on the game farm where he now resides, and the site of many of the assaults. Apparently he has also funded a children's home in the area.

Press Release:


Sidney Frankel
He was South Africa’s most famous stockbroker. A pillar of society, his wealth and influence knew no bounds. But today, billionaire Sidney Frankel stands accused as a paedophile. Seven people have come forward taking Frankel on in court and alleging he sexually assaulted them as young children. Carte Blanche hears their stories and also speaks exclusively to an alleged victim going public for the first time.

Link: In its heyday in the 70’s and 80’s, Diagonal Street was at the heart of Johannesburg’s financial district, and the Frankel family’s stock broking firm was at the pinnacle of the wheeling and dealing that took place here, giving Sidney almost limitless access to wealth and influence.
V/O: In 1994 Frankel invited Nelson Mandela to visit the Johannesburg Stock Exchange. His visit brought trading to a standstill. But the glossy image of the biggest broker in the country would be tarnished 20 years later.
Nicci: My first prize would be to see Sidney Frankel go to prison, which is where I believe he belongs because he’s a danger to society.
V/O; 46- year old Nicci Levenstein is the first of seven plaintiffs claiming damages from Frankel in a civil lawsuit.
Nicky: He would take us to his horse-riding farm where I would be with a circle of young girls and boys.

I have very distinct memories of his voice, what his hands looked like and the watch that he wore. Paul: And he moves the Coke bottle up and down our penis, and the penis gets an erection, as it does.
George: He was my hero, so if he was telling me it’s ok for him to be touching my penis, then as a little boy I’m assuming it’s ok for him to be touching my penis.

Shane: An allegation was made by another girl, and she had come forward and said that Sidney had approached her in the bathroom and she had felt very uncomfortable about him entering that private space. Beach link: It would appear that much of Sidney Frankel’s life has been spent surrounded by children. But even here in Muizenberg on the beach, whilst on holiday, he managed to gain the trust of a child who alleges be abused her.

Bongani: How old were you?
Phoebe: I was 8. So it was acceptable for an adult to be around while you were changing and he once again touched me in the hut.
Bongani: Did you tell your mother what had happened?
Phoebe: I did not; I did not.
V/O: Phoebe claims the abuse continued over a period of 3 weeks.
Phoebe: I was stung by a bluebottle with them, and I was stung high up on my thigh - and for some unknown reason he decided that I needed to take my costume off, and that he needed to put a cream on the sting. And he felt that the entire area needed to have cream, so he rubbed cream into my vagina. That was the worst for me.

Phoebe: Ideally I’d love to see him go to jail.

V/O: But as our law currently stands, that may never happen, according to attorney Ian Levitt.
Ian: In our Criminal Procedures Act sexual offences is a crime that prescribes after 20 years. As you know these offences took place, some more than 30 years ago, and they do not have - as the law stands now - redress in the criminal court.
V/O: The plaintiffs are claiming R5 million each in damages from Sidney Frankel. But for them it’s not about the money.
Shane: I would give up the civil suit in a heartbeat if I could go back within the 20-year period that the law allows for to file a criminal charge.
V/O: But criminal charges have been laid against Sidney Frankel regardless.
Ian: Why should the 20-year period commence on the date of the offence in, from a criminal perspective, but in a civil claim you can bring it 35 years later? We expect that the National Director of Public Prosecutions will refuse to prosecute when a charge is laid, and that decision we will take on review to the Constitutional Court.
V/O: We tried to put these allegations to Sidney Frankel himself, but he refused to comment. And then he phoned us back.
Sidney: Hi is that Bongani?
Bongani: Yes it is.
Sidney: It’s Sidney Frankel, I just want to say I really appreciate you giving me the chance to respond. You’re the first press who have actually done that.
Bongani: What do you think is at the heart of this? Are you just being defamed here?
Sidney: I cant’; I cant answer. I cannot answer, I’ve been told don’t, this is complicated; just let it go through the proper court. And you’ve seen in all the press I haven’t answered.

Katherine: When I was about 28 Sidney confronted me, and he said to me "I’m going for therapy and part of my therapy is to ask that you forgive me for what I did to you." And I jut recall feeling so shocked! In my mind I thought what did you do to me?

Ian: In 2007 what happened was the bill called the 2007 Sexual Offences Act was passed. Now any penetration - it doesn’t have to be sexual intercourse - it can be anything, it can be any part of the body - that is now also considered rape. So today, what he did then would be rape today.
Lisa: I want him to acknowledge the damage that he’s cause us. I wasn’t him to understand that he stole my innocence; that he took my childhood innocence and he can never give it back.
Katherine: For him to realize that he hasn’t got away with the damage that he’s done to so many people.
Shane: I felt like a used thing. I tried that, didn’t’ enjoy it; move on to the next one.

Paul: No, because I’m also a broken man, I'm repairing myself and he must have the courage to come and face the people that he broke.

SIDNEY FRANKEL

He was a regular visitor at the Arcadia Jewish Children’s Home in Johannesburg. Shane: He certainly had his keen favourites. Bongani: Were you one of his favourites? Shane: No, and I think that it was an issue for me after my one or two engagements with him that weren’t so kosher or above board. I often wondered why I wasn’t one of the special kids? Bongani: They didn’t believe you? Shane: No, and his presence in and amongst the children continued. Link: For any welfare organization, particularly one that looks after vulnerable children, the interest of a wealthy philanthropist presents a golden opportunity. But not when he’s accused of being a paedophile. Shane: An allegation was made by another girl, and she had come forward and said that Sidney had approached her in the bathroom and she had felt very uncomfortable about him entering that private space. At that point, from what I can gather, his access to the children was terminated. Not just restricted, he was asked not to engage at all with the children, and then he stopped visiting. V/O: Arcadia Jewish Children’s Home confirmed that Sidney Frankel was barred from seeing the children in the early 90’s. Beach link: It would appear that much of Sidney Frankel’s life has been spent surrounded by children. But even here in Muizenberg on the beach, whilst on holiday, he managed to gain the trust of a child who alleges be abused her. Phoebe: He came to fetch me from my house and said no that his daughters were going to meet us at the beach and they never, ever arrived. Phoebe: I was 8. So it was acceptable for an adult to be around while you were changing and he once again touched me in the hut. Bongani: Did you tell your mother what had happened? Phoebe: I did not; I did not. V/O: Phoebe claims the abuse continued over a period of 3 weeks. Phoebe: I was stung by a bluebottle with them, and I was stung high up on my thigh - and for some unknown reason he decided that I needed to take my costume off, and that he needed to put a cream on the sting. Bongani: What would you like to see happen? Phoebe: Ideally I’d love to see him go to jail. V/O: But as our law currently stands, that may never happen, according to attorney Ian Levitt. Ian: In our Criminal Procedures Act sexual offences is a crime that prescribes after 20 years. As you know these offences took place, some more than 30 years ago, and they do not have - as the law stands now - redress in the criminal court. V/O: The plaintiffs are claiming R5 million each in damages from Sidney Frankel. But for them it’s not about the money. Shane: I would give up the civil suit in a heartbeat if I could go back within the 20-year period that the law allows for to file a criminal charge. V/O: But criminal charges have been laid against Sidney Frankel regardless. Ian: Why should the 20-year period commence on the date of the offence in, from a criminal perspective, but in a civil claim you can bring it 35 years later? We expect that the National Director of Public Prosecutions will refuse to prosecute when a charge is laid, and that decision we will take on review to the Constitutional Court. V/O: We tried to put these allegations to Sidney Frankel himself, but he refused to comment. And then he phoned us back. Sidney: Hi is that Bongani? Bongani: Yes it is. Sidney: It’s Sidney Frankel, I just want to say I really appreciate you giving me the chance to respond. You’re the first press who have actually done that. Bongani: What do you think is at the heart of this? Are you just being defamed here? Sidney: I cant’; I cant answer. I cannot answer, I’ve been told don’t, this is complicated; just let it go through the proper court. And you’ve seen in all the press I haven’t answered. V/O: But according to Lisa Wegner, Frankel discussed the issue with her 12 years ago. Lisa: He said to me the reason he'd abused us was because his father had abused him as a child. He told me that he was in long-term therapy to deal with this. V/O; He told his cousin Katherine Rosenberg the same thing. Katherine: When I was about 28 Sidney confronted me, and he said to me "I’m going for therapy and part of my therapy is to ask that you forgive me for what I did to you." And I jut recall feeling so shocked! In my mind I thought what did you do to me? Bongani: You’re not sugar-coating this, you’re not calling it inappropriate behavior. You’re saying it’s rape? Ian: In 2007 what happened was the bill called the 2007 Sexual Offences Act was passed. Now any penetration - it doesn’t have to be sexual intercourse - it can be anything, it can be any part of the body - that is now also considered rape. So today, what he did then would be rape today. Lisa: I want him to acknowledge the damage that he’s cause us. I wasn’t him to understand that he stole my innocence; that he took my childhood innocence and he can never give it back. Katherine: For him to realize that he hasn’t got away with the damage that he’s done to so many people. Shane: I felt like a used thing. I tried that, didn’t’ enjoy it; move on to the next one. Bongani: If Sidney was here, sitting across from you, what would you say to him? Nicci: I would say to him that I'm so sorry that it took me so long to get to this point, because I’m just thinking about how many lives it would have impacted upon, and saved from what we had to go through. George: Stand up and be accountable for what you did. We know what you did, you know what you did, your whole family knows what you did. What I would say to him is the truth heals, and I’m sure you want healing. Bongani: Frankel’s said to be a broken man, he’s facing ill health. Does that move you in any way? Paul: No, because I’m also a broken man, I'm repairing myself and he must have the courage to come and face the people that he broke. SIDNEY FRANKEL Promo 1: (10”) V/O: Billionaire Sidney Frankel is a paedophile, according to family. Katherine: My most vivid memory is of him having me in his car with him, and his hand between my legs. Promo 2: (15”) V/O: Is billionaire Sidney Frankel a paedophile? Lisa: I should have told him stop. But I didn’t; I couldn’t; I didn’t have a voice. Paul: I did nothing wrong. I arrived as a kid, a great kid, and advantage was taken of me. Promo 3: (15”) V/O: Alleged paedophile Sidney Frankel faces a damages claim. But what do his accusers really want? Shane: For me the ideal way would be for a criminal court to acknowledge to the world at large: what you did was criminal.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Will one of South Africa's best known stockbrokers is be remembered as South Africa's worst paedophile?
metadata.Summary: Rich and powerful, stockbroker Sidney Frankel is being sued by 7 complainants who accuse him of having sexually abused them when they were children. Since the case became public, more victims have come forward, swelling the total to 24.
metadata.Further information: Criminal charges of rape will be laid against Sidney Frankel. Because the offence is alleged to have happened over 20 years ago the complainant expects the prosecutor to decline to prosecute. When that happens the Sexual Offences Act of 2007 will be challenged in the Constitutional Court.
metadata.Extra Budget Items: Travel to Cape Town to interview victims and to film the huts at Muizenberg beach, the site of many of the assaults Travel to Hoedspruit to find Sidney Frankel on the game farm where he now resides, and the site of many of the assaults. Apparently he has also funded a children's home in the area.
